chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The man must not swear an oath except based upon his knowledge.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a valid oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores that the validity of an oath hinges on the swearer's certainty (yaqin), distinguishing it from mere belief or speculation. It serves as a foundational principle for avoiding perjury (ghasir) and ensures that oaths carry legal weight in personal and communal matters, reflecting the high ethical standard of truthfulness emphasized by the Imams.
